parsed.summary: The formalization proves two things. First, there is a finite connected bipartite 2-degenerate graph H on Fin q, in which every proper 2-colouring has a vertex of degree ≥3 in each colour class, and constants c, ε > 0 with ex(n,H) ≥ c·n^{3/2+ε} for all sufficiently large n. Second, the statement 'every bipartite r-degenerate graph H has ex(n,H) = O(n^{2−1/r})' is false. Both match Theorem 1.2 and the refutation of Erdős's degeneracy conjecture, with the first slightly stronger than the paper. The main caveat is coverage: Theorem 1.1 (failure of compactness) is not formalized at all.

glossary.plain: N_s(v) = {u ∈ s : u ~ v}, the neighbours of v inside the finite set s
glossary.standard_concept: neighbourhood restricted to a vertex subset

glossary.plain: Every nonempty finite vertex set s contains a vertex v with |N_s(v)| ≤ r
glossary.note: Stated via induced subgraphs on finite sets. For finite graphs this is equivalent to the paper's 'every nonempty subgraph has a vertex of degree ≤ r'.

glossary.plain: For all r, q and every bipartite r-degenerate graph H on Fin q, ex(n,H) = O(n^{2−1/r}) as n→∞
glossary.note: For r=0, 1/0 = 0 in Lean, so the exponent becomes 2 and the bound is trivially true; this is harmless. The hypothesis 0 ≤ r is vacuous for r : ℕ.

lean_claims.plain: There exist q and a simple graph H on Fin q with all of the following properties. (i) H is connected. (ii) H is bipartite. (iii) H is 2-degenerate. (iv) For every proper 2-colouring of H and each colour, some vertex of that colour has degree > 2; in particular both colour classes are nonempty. (v) There are reals c, ε > 0 with c·n^{3/2+ε} ≤ ex(n,H) for all sufficiently large n.
There exist r ∈ ℕ and a bipartite r-degenerate finite graph H such that ex(n,H) is not O(n^{2−1/r}).

paper_claims.plain: There is a finite nonempty family F of connected bipartite graphs, each containing a cycle, with ex(n,F) = O(n^{4/3−1/48}) and ex(n,F) = Ω(n^{4/3}) for each F ∈ F.
There exist a fixed connected bipartite 2-degenerate H and c, ε > 0 with ex(n,H) ≥ c·n^{3/2+ε} for all sufficiently large n.
Not every bipartite r-degenerate H has ex(n,H) = O(n^{2−1/r}); this already fails for r = 2.

coverage.why: Contains everything in Theorem 1.2 plus an extra conjunct: each colour class of every 2-colouring has a vertex of degree ≥3.
This is the direct negation of conjecture (3) as stated in the paper.
The compactness counterexample is absent from the Lean file.

flags.explanation: The failure-of-compactness result (the family F with ex(n,F) = O(n^{4/3−1/48})) is not formalized.

The extra conjunct says every colour class has maximum degree > 2. Because Finset.sup of an empty set is 0, it also forces both classes to be nonempty. This makes Lean stronger than the paper, and it rules out the known solved case where one class has max degree ≤ r.

For r=0, 1/(0:ℝ) = 0, giving exponent 2, so the r=0 instance is trivially true. The hypothesis 0 ≤ r is vacuous. Neither point makes the negated statement easier, since the counterexample must come from r ≥ 1. For r=1 the graphs are forests with ex = O(n), so the r=1 instance cannot supply a cheap counterexample either.
flags.probe_idea: Prove that DegeneracyConjectureStatement restricted to r = 1 holds, or prove the r = 2 instance is false directly from twoDegenerateExtremalCounterexample.
